I am 55 years old and have farmed these 3.8 mu in Quzhou for 30 years. My wife and I are the only two workers in our household, so I cannot afford complicated or labor-heavy plans. We have a well, which means we can irrigate when needed, but pumping costs electricity, so I do not waste water.

For **winter wheat**, I will sow around October 10th. I always use an improved variety like Jimai — not the most expensive seed, but reliable. I need about 30 jin of seed per mu. Before sowing, I will rotary-till the field to break up the wheat stubble from the previous maize season and level the ground. For fertilizer, I will spread compound fertilizer (the special wheat formula, around 18-22-5) as a basal application — about 100 jin per mu — and then topdress with urea at the jointing stage in spring. In total, that comes to about 20 kg of nitrogen, 10 kg of phosphorus, and 5 kg of potassium per mu. I will irrigate three times: once right after sowing to ensure good germination, once at green-up/jointing, and once at grain filling. If the winter is unusually dry, I might add a winter irrigation, but three times is usually enough for our soil. For crop protection, I will spray herbicide once after sowing and apply insecticide twice for aphids and other pests. That is three pesticide applications in total. I expect about 500 kg per mu — not a record yield, but steady and enough for us.

For **summer maize**, the window between wheat harvest and sowing is only about a week, so there is no time for plowing. I will use the no-tillage seeder directly after the wheat combine leaves the field. I plant hybrid maize, about 1.2 packages per mu. I put compound fertilizer (the 28-6-6 type) down with the seeder as a basal dose of about 100 jin per mu, then topdress with urea at the big trumpet stage. This gives roughly 18 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, and 5 kg potassium per mu. Maize needs less irrigation than wheat here; I will irrigate twice — once after sowing if the soil is dry, and once during filling. For pests, I spray herbicide once and insecticide twice for armyworm and aphids, so three applications total. I expect about 550 kg per mu.

This is the system I have used for decades. Fertilizer prices have risen, so I do not over-apply, but cutting back too much hurts the yield. With just two of us, this plan is manageable and gives a reliable income.
